messages:
mira: opened a micro-PR to add a backpressure example and a generator-style Python streaming snippet to the SDK docs. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/940
otavio: nice. generator-style? can you show the python snippet here so i can verify it's idiomatic?
mira: sure, kept it tiny and explicit about cooperative backpressure and cancellation:
```python
# python generator-based stream with cooperative backpressure
from redwood import Client

def stream_generator(prompt):
    client = Client()
    with client.stream("gpt-open-1", prompt=prompt) as s:
        for chunk in s:
            yield chunk.text

# consumer can pause by controlling iteration rate
for token in stream_generator("hello"):
    process(token)
```
ben: I like that. add a short note saying this sync generator is for simpler sync apps; show async iterator separately.
harper: also add a tiny example of handling transient errors with a retry wrapper around the generator consumer, and mention not to retry inside the stream itself to avoid duplicating tokens.
mira: good point. i'll add a consumer-side retry wrapper and a small paragraph about idempotence and partial responses.
docs-bot: Reminder: please include snippet-validation in PR (mypy/flake8 for py, tsc --noEmit for TS, go vet for Go) or mark waived in the PR body. CI will enforce. :robot_face:
otavio: for the TS side i'll convert existing streaming example to await-for-await and include a note on backpressure (e.g., using async-iterator consumer delays).
mira: i've also fixed two broken links in the streaming guide (examples/streaming-old -> examples/streaming). added a brief migration note: "prefer consumer-side retry and backoff; avoid re-sending partial input when retrying".
ben: once you add the consumer retry sample and the CI lint job, i'm happy to approve. aim to keep examples copy-paste small so they fit in the docs code panes.
mira: will do. merging after lint job passes. thanks! :thumbsup:
